name: Question 3
problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,i-\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,j$ at an arbitrary point where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$
worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)\,j \\  & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,i-2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)^{2}+(-2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{sin}^{2}⁡2t+4{cos}^{2}⁡2t} \\  & =\sqrt{4({sin}^{2}⁡2t+{cos}^{2}⁡2t)} \\  & =\sqrt{4} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,i-2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,j) \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,i-\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3

Find the unit tangent vector to the curve r(t)=cos⁡2ti−sin⁡2tj at an arbitrary point where t∈(−∞,∞).

a
12(−sin⁡2ti−cos⁡2tj)
b
2sin⁡2ti−cos⁡2tj
c
−sin⁡2ti−cos⁡2tj
d
12(sin⁡2ti−cos⁡2tj)
e
2(−sin⁡2ti+cos⁡2tj)
Submit

EXPLANATION

For a curve r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j, the unit tangent vector T(t) at the point P(x(t),y(t)) is given by T(t)=r′(t)‖r′(t)‖.

First, we find the derivative of r(t):

r′(t)=ddt(cos⁡2t)i+ddt(−sin⁡2t)j=−2sin⁡2ti−2cos⁡2tj

Next, we calculate the magnitude of r′(t):

‖r′(t)‖=(−2sin⁡2t)2+(−2cos⁡2t)2=4sin2⁡2t+4cos2⁡2t=4(sin2⁡2t+cos2⁡2t)=4=2

Finally, we normalize r′(t) and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

T(t)=r′(t)‖r′(t)‖=12(−2sin⁡2ti−2cos⁡2tj)=−sin⁡2ti−cos⁡2tj
